title: WEB Terminal
description:
[h1]WEB Terminal — a live terminal as your wallpaper[/h1]

A real, working terminal on your desktop: run btop, htop, tmux, vim, a build log, an AI coding agent or a server console and keep it in view all day. It is not a recording or a fake, it is a live shell.

[b]IMPORTANT: this wallpaper needs its own small backend running on a machine you control.[/b] Wallpaper Engine can't start shell sessions by itself, so a tiny open-source program (the backend) runs the shell and the wallpaper connects to it. Without it you will see a "No connection to the backend" card. Setup takes about two minutes, see below.

[h2]What it is good for[/h2]
[list]
[*] A living dashboard: btop, htop, glances, logs, tail -f, watch, docker stats
[*] Watching long builds, tests, deployments or AI agents work while you do something else
[*] A server console: connect the backend on a home server, VM or Raspberry Pi and see it on your desktop
[*] A beautiful, themed terminal as a backdrop for streams and screenshots
[/list]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Real pty shell (bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell, WSL, anything you configure) via xterm.js
[*] Images in the terminal: Kitty graphics protocol (kitten icat, chafa and similar)
[*] Works with the left mouse button only: a radial quick menu (copy, paste, clear, Ctrl+C, scroll, font size, theme, background opacity, keyboard) and a built-in on-screen keyboard with several layouts
[*] Several colour themes, bundled fonts (JetBrains Mono and more), adjustable font size and background opacity
[*] Menu button position, size and opacity, menu language (29 languages) are configurable
[*] Shows a helpful message with the most common causes when the backend is unreachable
[*] Fully local: no external requests, all fonts and libraries are bundled
[/list]

[h2]Quick setup[/h2]
[olist]
[*] Get the backend: download the build for your system (Windows, Linux, macOS; x64 and ARM64) from [url=https://github.com/erophey7/we-terminal-backend/releases/latest]the latest release[/url]. Source code and build instructions: [url=https://github.com/erophey7/we-terminal-backend]github.com/erophey7/we-terminal-backend[/url]
[*] Create webterm.yml next to it (see config.example.yml in the repository). Minimal example:
[code]
listen:
  ip: 127.0.0.1
  port: 3000
auth:
  enabled: true
  token: "a-long-random-secret"
access:
  allowed_origins: ["file://"]
[/code]
[*] Start the backend from the folder that contains webterm.yml (it is read from the current directory; or pass the path as the first argument):
[code]
# Windows (PowerShell; in cmd drop the "./")
./webterm-windows-amd64.exe

# Linux
chmod +x webterm-linux-amd64
./webterm-linux-amd64

# macOS (Apple Silicon)
chmod +x webterm-darwin-arm64
./webterm-darwin-arm64

# custom config path
./webterm-linux-amd64 /path/to/webterm.yml
[/code]
The startup log shows the listen address and the allowed origins; leave the window open while you use the wallpaper. Windows SmartScreen / macOS Gatekeeper may warn because the binaries are not code-signed. To start it automatically with your system, see the deployment guide in the backend repository.
[*] In the wallpaper properties set the backend address (default ws://localhost:3000/pty) and the same token.
[*] Click the menu button in the corner of the wallpaper for quick actions.
[/olist]
Detailed guide (including configuring a shell, WSL, Linux/macOS, running as a service): see the repositories below.

[h2]Security — please read[/h2]
The backend gives access to a shell. Keep it bound to 127.0.0.1 (or a trusted LAN), always set a token, and never expose it to the internet. The wallpaper itself never stores anything outside Wallpaper Engine's own settings.

[h2]Source code and licenses[/h2]
[list]
[*] Wallpaper (this project): [url=https://github.com/erophey7/we-terminal]github.com/erophey7/we-terminal[/url]
[*] Backend: [url=https://github.com/erophey7/we-terminal-backend]github.com/erophey7/we-terminal-backend[/url]
[*] Both are open source under permissive licences (see LICENSE in each repository). Bundled components: xterm.js and its addons (MIT) and fonts (SIL OFL 1.1); the full list is in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md and vendor/licenses/ inside the wallpaper folder.
[/list]

Issues and suggestions are welcome on GitHub.

autocopyselection.text: Copy to clipboard on mouse selection

keyboard.text: On-screen keyboard (button in the radial menu)

menusize.text: Menu button: size in px (0 = automatic, scales with the screen)

token.text: Auth token (if enabled on the backend)
